scripted_split.about: Scripted songs only (a song opts in with "sentence_split": "scripted" in its knobs.json). The song engine splits each line once, joins the pieces with segment_marker (an invisible character), and both the robot (one say per piece) and the chat bubble (one highlight per piece) split on it. A piece ends at one of piece_ends (. ! ? and, since 2026-10-01, the comma) before a space - a comma inside a quote does not end one; an ellipsis (... or …) never ends a piece, so "Ah... I like to party" stays whole; a closing quote stays with its piece; a trailing tag from join_trailing joins the piece before it.

live_split.about: Live chat replies: Wire-Pod says a reply one piece at a time and the chat bubble lights the same pieces (operator 2026-10-06: "aim for a hard split between sentences ... within each sentence, split by comma ... forget minimum word rules ... simplify"). Sentences first: one ends at any of sentence_ends before a space (never at an ellipsis), or at a line break. Then, inside each sentence, a piece ends at any of comma_ends before a space, or at an ellipsis. No length rules: a one-word sentence is a piece. gopod_speech_sentences.go.
live_split.smooth_about: 2026-10-15 (operator: 'keep commas, smoothen choppiness'; 'Longer sentences with nice pauses, as per: "At every step the robot pauses less, the reveal shows a bigger piece at once, and the chat scrolls less."'; 'thought bubble = paragraph'; 'go ahead with revised step 1'): join_up_to_words 25 - a sentence of up to 25 words is said whole, its commas the robot's own pauses; a longer one splits at its commas; short pieces in a row join up to 25 words. thought_lines - each thought on its own line (the code's start and end lines, and gemma's emoji-closed thoughts), and a run never crosses into the next thought.
live_split.thought_lines_about: 2026-10-16 (operator: "please add a line between thought bubbles ... please apply globally, thought bubbles as (spaced) paragraphs"): on again, with join_up_to_words 0 - each thought is its own paragraph with a blank line between, highlighting stays per pause (comma pieces).
live_split.join_about: 2026-10-08 (operator: "less choppiness in responses ... very short comma filled sentences ... sound choppy and annoying ... a few sentences in a row sound smoother"): after the split, a piece takes in the next while the two together are at most join_up_to_words words, so short sentences and comma pieces are said - and lit - as one run. 0: no joining (the 2026-10-06 split as it was). A playing draft's move phrases (lift my arm, nod, test my cube) stay their own pieces, so each move still lands on its words.

countdown.about: A short countdown in the Brobots window while the rattle's hand-off and sound run (operator 2026-10-01: "after please wait, add a countdown timer in the brobots window"). The song posts one chat-feed line from role with the seconds; the page counts it down and removes it. Not kept in chat memory. rattle_sound_seconds is the rattle's own length, added to the engine's settle wait to make the count. Since 2026-10-04 (operator: "have visuals respond to what's there") the song posts end_text from role when the rattle has really finished, and the page removes the timer then; the seconds are only a fallback (plus 10 s) if that line never comes.

chat_hold.about: The Brobots stay in place while chatting (operator 2026-10-04: "Hold both Brobots between answers", "I should have a thanks brobots cue to re-engage"). After a chat answer both Brobots are held under behavior control (DEFAULT priority, the songs' own hold) so they don't wander; each is let go while he answers or defers. "Thanks Brobots" (said or typed; any of thanks_phrases, whole words) gets a party-bro sign-off from the Brobot that answers (thanks_note is added before the question), then ends the hold and both go back to free play (operator 2026-10-04: "Can the brobots give me a party-brobot response, that also triggers the release"); so does idle_minutes with no question. A song or alias that assumes a robot's control through Wire-Pod takes over from the hold.
chat_hold.thanks_note: [Not a question - Brobot 0 is thanking the Brobots and wrapping up the chat. Give a short, fun party-bro sign-off, and don't ask anything back.]
chat_hold.stuck_about: A Brobot that drops off mid-answer (froze, rebooted, out of Wi-Fi) left his answer waiting forever, so after he came back nothing he wrote was spoken (operator 2026-10-06: "clear stuck brobot state to reconnect ... like upon a rebooted brobot"). Now one sentence or move that takes longer than stuck_seconds ends that answer: the chat page drops its outline, the hold and Record Session carry on, and his next question works without wpr 2. Log line: GOPOD_STUCK_REPLY.

chat_moves.about: Each chat reply gets one small move with its first mid-reply animation (gopod_arm_cue.go): the arm cue (each robot's phcal-tuned lift), or - every nod_every-th reply of that Brobot - a head nod instead (operator 2026-10-04: "I notice arm lifts throughout responses - add nods to replace some arm lifts?"). The nod is the songs' own: head down at nod_speed for nod_hold_seconds, back up the same, then stop (phcal_last.json nod: speed 4, hold 0.18).
chat_moves.searching_about: 2026-10-08: while a Brobot waits on his answer he plays the searching clip every searching_interval_seconds until the answer is ready, as before, and now for at least searching_min_seconds (operator: "a required minimum run to act as a buffer against an early trigger, whether composing a response, or not"), then one searchingGetout. A draft answer is ready at once, so it gets exactly the minimum, after "Thinking, please wait."
chat_moves.searching_resend_about: After the first searching_min_seconds, the clip is sent again no sooner than searching_resend_seconds - one clip's length (go search V7 gesture_clip_ms 3918), the golden rule that it's never re-sent faster than it plays (SEARCHING_ANIMATION_SONG_LOCK_001.md). It still ends the moment the answer is ready.
chat_moves.thinking_moves_about: Operator 2026-10-09: "For the thinking please wait sequence * for live and scripted * start with an arm lift + nod (as visual cues to the audience) * then the rest". Done in this order before Thinking, please wait., each back at rest before the next (arm: the phcal arm cue; nod: nod_speed / nod_hold_seconds). Empty: none.
chat_moves.thinking_text_about: 2026-10-18 (operator: "\"thinking please wait\" process * replace with short & sweet: \"Got it!\"").
chat_moves.got_it_about: 2026-10-24 (operator: "Separate out the already established, locked, golden 'Got it' sequence, & duplicate * assign Got it 1 to brobot 1 * assign Got it 2 to brobot 2"): each Brobot's own copy of the golden sequence - his moves (arm, nod), his words, then his searching pace. Both start as exact copies of the golden values above; a part left out takes the golden one. Needs wpr 2.
chat_moves.animation_timing_about: Operator 2026-10-09: "Use playAnimationWI + 0.9s + start speech * no new animations until enough time has lapsed for playAnimationWI run completion, or a 'done' message is received". In a reply (live and scripted), the speech after a playAnimationWI starts speech_after_animation_seconds after the animation was sent; the next animation waits until the robot reports the one before it done, never longer than animation_done_most_seconds.
chat_moves.speech_after_animation_seconds_about: 2026-10-24 (operator: "between spoken segments there's a 0.9s delay * can the run timings be adjusted to fire the next spoken segment 0.5s early?"): was 0.9 (2026-10-09, playAnimationWI + 0.9s + start speech), now 0.4. Needs wpr 2.

bingo_ball.about: A big Bingo ball in the Brobots window for each called number (operator 2026-10-02: "make a really big bingo ball number display for B-1, I-9 & O-0"). A song step with "show_ball": "B-1" in its knobs.json posts one chat-feed line from role with the number when the step starts; the page shows the ball and keeps it in the chat window (operator 2026-10-04: "Please keep the bingo balls displayed"); only Clear Chat removes it. Not kept in chat memory. The ball's colour follows its letter (B I N G O).

sounds_on_about: Where Wire-Pod's playSound sounds play (danger-will-robinson.wav, kgsim_cmds.go): "page" - the Brobots chat page plays them like a reporter voice (operator 2026-10-09: "keep but pause playing through the brobot, too much trouble now * instead make it play through the web page like the reporter voices ... same with danger wav"); "robot" - streamed to the robot, as before. The Bingo test's rattle has its own knob (rattle_on in its knobs.json, "page" now).
page_sound_files_about: 2026-10-10: a song's own soundtrack (its knobs.json "audio") is now found by the song and copied without being listed here (gopod_song_folders.go). This list is for any other sound. Extra sound files Wire-Pod copies into the page's voice folder at its start, beside sounds/*.wav (relative to the overlay's chipper folder): a song's private soundtrack. A missing file is logged and skipped (the media isn't in the public repo).

page_text.about: 2026-10-29 (operator: "sweep for all flexible data, variables, names, labels, etc and export to external files ... then code blindly runs templates from loaded files"): the chat page's own words - its typing row, the system window's panels. {placeholders} are filled by the page.
page_text.typed_placeholder: Type to the Brobot, press Enter

chat_window.about: The chat bubbles window's timings and sizes (operator 2026-10-18: "ensure flexible data/info values/variables are in loadable files (css, js, json, md, etc...) * code is dumb flow guiding machine"), read by the page on F5: max_bubbles/max_seen - the saved chat; baton_max_ms - the longest a bubble waits for the one above to finish; bubble_ready_max_ms - for its pictures to load; reply_delay_ms - a reply after its question; top_gap_px - space above the newest bubble; scroll_ms - one scroll; focus_dead_zone - how far the highlight may drift before the chat follows (share of the window); countdown_hold_ms / countdown_hold_most_ms - the next line after a countdown; voice_lit_wait_ms - a reporter/Goverlord line's words show anyway after this with no voice; marquee_* - the egg bulbs; narrator_fade_* - the narrator bubbles' fades (seconds); reveal_rest_ms - a reply's rest shows after this with no more highlight.
chat_window.voice_lit_wait_ms_about: 2026-10-30 (CLOCK_AUDIT_001.md, live 15:48: CHALK's long answer's voice took 22 s to make; at 15 s his words showed whole, before his voice): a voiced line waits for its own voice - Wire-Pod says "off" when one fails; this is only the guard against a hang. 15000 -> 120000.
chat_window.speaking_max_ms_about: 2026-10-18 (operator: "Fix the leak. Fix all leaks."): a line still lit after this long (a robot that froze, a lost end signal) no longer holds the next bubble back.
chat_window.voice_ready_max_ms_about: 2026-10-23: the longest a shown line's voice waits for its length and word times before it plays anyway.
chat_window.picture_wait_about: 2026-10-24 (operator: "All chat bubbles * aim to render and display a shell bubble + placeholders * [hourglass per image]/display image(s)"): a picture still loading shows as an hourglass in its place; one not made yet (a slow Easter egg's photo) is asked for again every picture_retry_ms, at most picture_wait_max_ms. F5.
chat_window.typed_text_min_px_about: 2026-10-23 (operator: "New responsive Brobots-Input-Row single line can adjust to 3 lines"): the narrowest the text field may get on one line; narrower, the row takes three lines.

bubble_kinds.about: 2026-10-22 (operator: "Goverlord orchestrates * Gomads do most of the thinking * Gominions do with little to no thinking * There is a chain of command * There should be 5 bubbles essentially now: 1) Operator: input 2) Goverlord: System 3) Gomads: Managers help & are chat participants - unless called upon directly, gomads manage within a brobot bubble notice-bubble 4) Gominions: Performing brobots + output 5) Other: easter eggs, etc..."): every bubble in the chat gets one kind (data-tier), by its classes - the first rule that matches ([own] = the operator's own line). One with no kind is logged once (GOPOD_CHECK bubble without a kind) - a loose chain to place. Page only: F5.

hourglass.about: 2026-10-23 (operator: "animated hourglass: make sand empty from top/fill the bottom, then loop from top"): the Generating hourglass - steps frames from full top to full bottom, step_ms each, hold_ms full at the bottom, then from the top again. Page only: F5.

skip_gate.about: 2026-10-22 (operator: "skip is set to disabled * only upon voices ready can skip be enabled * upon skipped, 'skip' skip is set to disabled * otherwise template this everywhere"): every skip (Esc, numpad *, the menu's skip, typed or spoken "skip") goes through this gate - off until a warm-up line starting with one of enable_on shows (every warm-up song's "Voices ready.", the opener's too), off again once used. A skip while off does nothing (logged: skip ignored). Page only: F5.
skip_gate.about_2: 2026-10-25 (operator: "enable happens at \"Voices ready for playback.\" independent of edits"): no words matched any more - Wire-Pod opens the gate as the opener's message step right after the voice files check (wait_voices) shows (gopod_opener_song.go, feed line skip_on), whatever its words.

brobot_bubble.about: 2026-10-22 (operator: "TEMPLATE IT ALL OUT!!"): GOLDEN - the Brobot Bubble, one shape for every live answer, Brobot 1 and 2 alike, in this order. header: "Brobot N:" (+ the zoomable weather picture top right, its sound again on a click after its first play). got_it: he says chat_moves.thinking_text - notice line 1. value_points: notice line 2 (bubble_notices.value_points: points, search, none). manager: notice line 3 - a manager whose take his line asks for (managers.takes, native.to_manager) steps in now, while his answer is written; his searching waits; the manager's line uses the Generating template; a take with brobot_says leaves the result to him. thanks: notice line 4 - after a manager, he says got_it_again ("Thanks for your help, {helper}."). reply: his answer-chained reply (answer_chains; a weather question opens with the golden weather line). A step left out of steps is skipped (manager, thanks); got_it, value_points and reply always run.

gravity.about: 2026-10-22 (operator: "remember the gravitational pull to reveal all value points * please template this somewhere in the flow, lol * kinda like 'Back on track'"; GOPOD = a game of query for value points - however far it's pushed, it steers back): the pull, in every Brobot answer's flow - 1. his prompt's pre-build context names his reminders-list (prebuild_context: the points still to say); 2. his notice names them - "Back on track: ..." after a free answer, "Next up: ..." after a topic answer (bubble_notices.value_points.recovery / next); 3. his reply ends steering to them - "Hey, that reminds me..." (answer_chains reminder part for a free answer, the reminder end line for a topic answer; no dice). All three name the same points (gopodReminderLine).

bubble_notices.about: 2026-10-22 (operator: "make standard, the Notice-bubble inside a Brobot's bubble"; "template out what goes in a notice-bubble"): what goes in each notice at the top of a Brobot's bubble (the bubble notice template, gopodBubbleNotice: a title, then its lines, each on its own row; a notice with the same title takes more lines underneath). value_points: every live Brobot answer - what his answer is built from, that the GOPOD reps are hired to reveal - its parts in this order: points (one per value point given: {id} topic#n, {words}), weather ({line}), search ({search}), none (no value point), got_it ({thinking_text} = chat_moves.thinking_text, added once he has said it). egg: a found egg ({title}, {summary}). native_intent: a native Wire-Pod intent ({intent}). An empty title = that notice is off; a part left out of parts isn't shown.

value_points.title_about: 2026-10-30 (operator: "Rename Value Points to [persona-(nick)name] Brain * Brobot 1: Brain, CHALK: Brain, etc... * NEW CORE TEMPLATE RULE: everybody gets a brain bubble"): {name} is the persona's.
value_points.title: {name} Brain
value_points.log_about: 2026-10-25 (operator: "move these brobots spoken parts, out of notice-bubble, into and as part of the brobot response"): his opener (Got it! / Nice try, ...!) is no longer a notice line - it opens his response bubble (gopodOpenerFirst); the notice still waits for it to be said. 2026-10-22 (operator's notice log): 1. got_it - "Got it!" as he says it (the communication received); 2. points (y) or none (n), with search when there was one; 3. (optional) a manager's part - its header and line on one row, then its Generating line; while it talks the Brobot's searching waits; 4. got_it_again - when the floor comes back to him after a manager's part, he says and shows it (2026-10-22, operator: "instead, brobot says 'Thanks for you help, [Brobot N].'"; {helper} from helper_from); second_got_it after_manager, or off. Then his answer-chained reply below the notice.
value_points.game_about: 2026-10-22 (operator: "Game survey: 1-4"; GAME_FEEL_SURVEY_001.md - a game of query for value points, nothing outrageous): combo (points from two topics in one answer), chapter (a chapter's points all said - once), recovery (a free answer: the next points on the list), score (points said of them all). egg: one notice per bubble - an egg found for his line is a line here, not a notice of its own. note: a point's notes (its topic's notes N: line), each on its own line. Empty text = off.
value_points.notes_about: 2026-10-26 (operator: "to save vertical screen space list by \"|\" separator in a single line: [good Afternoon|classroom|kids shout wordplay at us|we respond back]"): a point's notes on one line under its title, joined with notes_join. Empty = one note per line (note).
value_points.guide_about: 2026-10-27 (operator: "Pretend everytime a notice-bubble appears in a brobot's response bubble, what would you tell my brobots to do at each call in the chat? * Or if you entered a GOPOD chat, how would you self-aware yourself, follow the chat and respond accordingly? * Set up a templated format like that?"; "Do as per example 'Next up' -> 'don't reveal these yet'"): for each notice line this answer shows, what he's told to do about it - in his pre-build context ({notice}, prebuild_context.lines), in parts order. {line} is the notice's own line. Empty or missing = not told (plan and score are their own pre-build lines; the point itself is in his facts).

guide.summary: {line} - give it as a short summary, your way.
guide.search: {line} - the results show with your answer: use them, never read them out.
guide.combo: {line} - tie them together in one answer.
guide.none: {line} - one or two sentences, then bridge back to GOPOD.
guide.recovery: Back on track with: {line} - pick one, don't reveal them all.

value_points.points_about: 2026-10-23 (operator: "should read as; a day of parties #3 of 3: Evening * expand to: #3 of 3 (template #[N] of [N])"): {total} = the topic's points.
value_points.template_2_about: 2026-10-25 (operator: "NEW TEMPLATE: Response-chain ... * No value point - a quick take, then back on track: * [topics] * Topics [score line] * Value Points [score line] * Easter Eggs [score line] * score lines vertically aligned"): none ends with the lead-in, recovery is the topics alone on the next line, score is three lines - each label, a tab, its bar (the page lines the bars up).
value_points.none: No value point - a quick take, then back on track:
value_points.helper_from_about: 2026-10-27: call_name first - host_personas.<host>.call_name, the name others call him by ("Thanks for your help, Cache PYC."). 2026-10-22 (operator: "Use gomad name ('Thanks for your help, PLAYHEAD.') * if no name available, fallback to brobot N * template this"): where {helper} comes from, first that has one: name (the manager's own name, PLAYHEAD / CHALK), brobot (its Brobot, managers.personas reporter: Brobot 4 / Brobot 3).

page_sync.about: Step 3, the engine conducts (operator 2026-10-18: "Finish Step 3"; the plan: "Wire-Pod decides order and timing. The page shows what it's told and answers shown, played and heard ... terminal and page run the same show, line for line"). reply_wait_seconds: a Brobot's reply goes on the feed, then he waits up to this long for the page to show his bubble before he speaks, so he never talks over a line the page is still playing (a page that's away isn't waited for; GOPOD_SYNC lines say when he waited or the page was behind). held_log_seconds: a line the page held longer than this before showing it (the bubble above, a countdown, the warm-up) is written to the journal (GOPOD_PAGE held). gopod_page_sync.go.
page_sync.main_lease_seconds_about: 2026-10-23 (C1, one page owns the show): the main page plays the sound and its reports time the run; every other page is a silent viewer. Gone longer than this (s), the next page that can play takes over.
page_sync.feed_max_about: 2026-10-24 (the root-to-leaf pass, link 2): the chat feed - the one line everything the page shows comes from, numbered - keeps its newest this many lines.
page_sync.second_admin_text_about: 2026-10-29 (operator: "I should only have one admin page open, correct? * add a check for one admin controller page * visitor pages are multiple"): shown in a second admin page's text field - it stays a silent viewer; Wire-Pod logs it (GOPOD_PAGE second admin page) and system-status counts the admin pages open.
page_sync.second_admin_text: Another admin page is open - this one only watches. Keep one admin page.
page_sync.display_about: 2026-10-24 (operator: "the visitor page does no thinking * visitor page zombie follows regardless of a nuclear war going on next door * visitor page zombie follows GOPOD admin feed"): the main page sends what it shows - its newest display_bubbles bubbles as drawn and where it's scrolled - at most every display_ms; every other page only paints that.
page_sync.item_max_ms_about: 2026-10-24 (live: the chat stopped after a reply until F5): a feed line that hasn't handed on after this long is logged (GOPOD_PAGE error stuck ...) and passed. F5.

chat_audio.about: 2026-10-14 (operator: "Rule: Please make all chat bubble audio default to volume variable to play at 10% volume * the background loop volume variable is set to play at 5% * all chat bubbles, system bubbles, reporter/narrator bubbles, brobots' chat bubbles, etc... * song sequences as well * Later, I may want to edit other play volumes as well"): every sound the chat page plays - voices, stings, a song's sounds and soundtrack, the weather sounds - plays at volume (0-1). 2026-10-14 (operator: "increase default volume from 10% to 35%"): 0.35. A sound's own volume (a sting's here, a song step's "volume") is its share of it: 1 = this volume, 0.8 = 80% of it. The background loop keeps its own volume (background_loop). The page reads it on F5.
chat_audio.master_about: 2026-10-17 (operator: "One master default knobs setting all other knobs refers to * other story.md knobs are either \"\" for default or \"0-100%\""): volume above is the master. Every other volume knob - a sting's, the numpad key sound, the weather sound, the background loop, a song step's \"volume\" - is \"\" (the master) or a percentage of it (\"40%\"); turning the master turns them all. An older bare number (0.4) still reads as 40%.
chat_audio.normalize_about: 2026-10-17 (operator: "evaluate audio files to normalize all volumes to -3db? * tag & apply a volume offset to the raw audio, before \"default\" knob setting"): every WAV in the voice folder is measured once (its loudest sample) and given the offset that brings it to normalize_db (gopod_audio_levels.go -> webroot/gopod_audio_levels.json); the page plays it at master x knob x offset. The files are never changed. 0 = off. The weather sounds (mp3) aren't measured.
chat_audio.loudness_about: 2026-10-17 (operator: "Measure by average loudness instead * include .mp3 weather sounds * include all sounds GOPOD uses"; "What I do in my audio editor is * I aim to adjustment a bit more than average loudness, to as close to but within the -3db range * then loudness over -3db I compress back to -3db * Can you do what I do instead"): every sound the chat plays is measured for its average loudness, turned to loudness_lufs, and whatever then goes over normalize_db is held back under it (ffmpeg's limiter, gopod_audio_levels.go). A made voice is done as it's made; every other sound (stings, song sounds, soundtracks, weather sounds) gets a done copy in webroot/gopod_audio_norm/ that the page plays instead - originals never changed. 0 = off.

background_loop.about: 2026-10-13 (operator: "a 6s loop * I want to run the loop in the background very quiet, try 10% volume * keyboard line record/session clock: upon any/every reset to 00:00:00 * ensure loop runs every 6s"): the chat page plays file (from the overlay's sounds/, copied to the page's voice folder at Wire-Pod's start) over and over with no gap, at volume (0-1), starting again from its top each time the session clock resets to 00:00:00. Empty file: off. 2026-10-17 (the master): volume is a percentage of chat_audio.volume - 0.05 on its own was 14% of 0.35.
background_loop.starts_on_about: 2026-10-24 (operator: "Page refresh now shows background loop speaker icon = ON, should be/it starts OFF"): the speaker on every page load - false, off (its volume bar shows only while it's on).

word_animations.about: The animation a spoken piece picks from its words (gopod_word_animations.go; animation_vocab.json's aliases: "party" -> celebrate, "mad" -> angry). Operator 2026-10-09: "its a joke/play on words, so the emotion should reflect that": a piece holding one of play_on_words (whole phrase, any case) gets play_on_words_animation instead. swap: an animation to replace with another in chat speech (empty: angry stays - operator 2026-10-09: "angry worked fine for many runs * keep it, just allow more time between animations", see chat_moves.animation_gap_seconds). Live and scripted answers both. Needs wpr 2.

system_bubble.about: The system bubbles' header (operator 2026-10-04: "label these timers as system messages ... [icon] Goverlord: GOPOD Brain [icon]"): every Goverlord system bubble (the LLM warm-up, countdowns, chapters, Goverlord's lines, numpad statuses), with the grey icon at both ends. Read by the chat page only.
system_bubble.label: Goverlord: GOPOD Brain

photo.about: The photo egg (operator 2026-10-14: "Get Photo in front of you ... implement anyways"; "describe the image simply * Example: I see a table, chair and some book shelves, or whatever, nothing crazy * refer to text descriptions used for photos already taken * store the image to then display in a web page * return control to the normal streaming loop * keep/snapshot the 3-2-1 countdown + mirror-mode + shutter animation, then lock as a golden process"; "treat these as found easter eggs throughout a live chat"). Live chat only. A line holding one of ask_phrases: the Brobot takes the photo the golden way (mirror mode, 3-2-1, shutter - Wire-Pod's own getImage), it pops up in his reply bubble (an egg, topic_pictures.max_per_session times; then a plain picture), Goverlord's congratulations, thinking please wait while vision_model (Ollama) looks at it with prompt, then answer_text with {saw}. One of recall_phrases: recall_text with what he saw last (nothing_text when he hasn't). No photo: fail_text; photo but no description: unclear_text. Photos are kept in webroot/photos (private, not in the repo). gopod_photo.go. 2026-10-14 test on this machine: SmolVLM2 2.2B ~3 s warm and good; moondream ~1.5 s but vague ("urns ... on a couch").
ask_phrases: what is in front of you
photo.vision_model_about: 2026-10-16 (operator: "Please continue with moondream for live photos"; a test: moondream was short and less wrong than SmolVLM2, which it replaces; "TEMPORARY RULE: No gemma4 or larger llm live switching").
photo.prompt: Describe what you see in one short, simple sentence, naming a few main things.
photo.nothing_text: I haven't taken a photo yet.
photo.unclear_text: I took a photo, but I couldn't make out what's in it.
photo.awake_seconds_about: 2026-10-14 (operator: "make sure brobots are awake, then 3-2-1, ... otherwise photo is taken as they're waking, head not in position"): after control is granted the Brobot waits this long - awake, head settled - before mirror mode and "3, 2, 1" (golden rule 3's settle, 1.5 s, plus time to finish waking).
photo.rounds_about: 2026-10-16 (operator: "Edge TPU list shown first while moondream is still looking (both, not a swap) * so do this in 2 rounds * round 1 is from TPU quick look (while moondream looks) * round 2 is from moondream"; then: "thinking please wait > photo > TPU > Brobot N: I see [TPU labels] * (if background moondream look still running, brobot says gathering details) * Brobot optional statement to stall for time * No bubble for notes ... this is background internal stuff * build brobot response as statement-2 'I see ... ...' from statement-1 & what moondream found"). The Brobot: Thinking, please wait. - the photo - the egg (egg_name) - the Edge TPU worker (quick_look, ~0.04 s) names the objects: statement 1, quick_text with {objects} (quick_none_text when it names none). vision_model looks meanwhile, in the background (its notes only in the log). After statement 1: gathering_text if it is still looking, then one of stall_lines if it is still looking; then statement 2: detail_text with {saw} - its own lead-in (detail_strip_prefixes) taken off, statement 1's objects it didn't name added; detail_unclear_text when it saw nothing. gopod_photo.go, gopod_photo_quick_look.go.

quick_look.about: The Edge TPU's object model (COCO, 90 kinds of thing). 2026-10-16 test on the kept photos: ssdlite_mobiledet at 0.4 named the most and right (person, chair, keyboard; ssd_mobilenet_v2 only one each; 0.3 added a wrong car). The Coral stick runs one program at a time - this worker holds it while Wire-Pod runs.
quick_look.pictures_about: 2026-10-17 (operator: "3 images displayed * [raw snapshot][snapshot enhancement attempt][TPU object recognition on enhancement] * I see ... [TPU read on enhancement] * I see ... [moondream read of TPU]"; "TPU with bounding boxes"): the worker cleans up the snapshot (enhance: median filter size, auto contrast cutoff %, then brightness, contrast, sharpness - 1 is unchanged), finds the objects in the enhanced one and draws their boxes and names; the egg pops up the photo, the enhanced one and the boxes; the vision model looks at the enhanced one, told the TPU's objects. Kept beside the photo (webroot/photos, _enhanced.jpg, _tpu.jpg).

math.about: The Brobots' math (operator 2026-10-14: "GOPOD is like as 'mathy' as math can get"; "gemma isn't for calculating"; "Build it all ... fractions, decimals, repeating decimals, same ground as fractions pack * Plus/minus/times/divide and percent * clean, correct & proper"; gopod_math.go). A math question in the live chat is worked out in code, exactly, and the Brobot answers it step by step, word for word - the LLM never calculates. Fraction to decimal (long division; a repeating block gets a bar, 0.3̅), decimal to fraction (over 10, 100, 1000..., simplified), repeating decimal to fraction (the 10x method), percents (to and from, '15% of 80', 'what percent is 3 of 4'), and plus, minus, times, divide with brackets and the order of operations. It reads digits and symbols and the speech-to-text's words ('zero point three repeating', 'three quarters'). lines: each step's words, {name} filled in; fractions show as 1⁄3 and are said 'over' (spoken_symbols). max_repeat_digits: a longer repeating block is shown rounded. Locked by TestMath*. 2026-10-14 (operator: "asking word, last? = 'Explain the Math' * same as livestream contest format: '[statement]. Explain the Math'"; "After 'Explain the Math', I'd like Brobot 1 to answer & Brobot 2 to follow up, Brobots shared-persona style"; "simple bullet list format"; "Wrap all that up as an 'Explain the Math' pop-up"): only a line that ends with trigger is math. Brobot 1 answers first, Brobot 2 follows up (whoever it was sent to): each says up to flavour_sentences of his own (the LLM's, any sentence with a number in it dropped), then his share of the steps, one bullet each - Brobot 2 the last third (at least the last step). In the live chat it's an 'Explain the Math' pop-up (popup_title over the challenge, Goverlord's congratulations; topic_pictures.max_per_session): Brobot 1's answer under the prize, Brobot 2's in his own marquee bubble (the pop-up rule, 2026-10-15: no 'Brobot N:' headers in pop-ups). 2026-10-15 (operator: "tell me about yourself vs tell me all about yourself * this feels like it should fall into a long 'math' response"): Explain the Math is the long answer - a fraction to decimal shows the long division itself, digit by digit (each bring-down, digit and remainder), until it ends or a remainder comes back, at most long_division_max_steps; a longer repeating block is said digit by digit ("the 1 4 2 8 5 7 repeats").

lines.fraction_divide: To turn {fraction} into a decimal, divide the top by the bottom: {top} ÷ {bottom}.
lines.division_repeats: {top} ÷ {bottom} = {decimal}. The remainder keeps coming back, so the {block} repeats forever.
lines.division_long: {top} ÷ {bottom} = {decimal}. It repeats, but its repeating block is too long to show.
lines.simplify: Divide the top and the bottom by {gcd}: {fraction} = {simple}.
lines.repeat_subtract: Subtract, and the repeating part cancels out: {bigx} − {smallx} = {big} − {small}, so {kx} = {diff}.
lines.times_hundred: To make a percent, times by 100: {decimal} × 100 = {percent}.
lines.common_bottom: Give them the same bottom, {bottom}: {a} = {a2}, and {b} = {b2}.
lines.times_fractions: Times the tops and times the bottoms: {a} × {b} = {result}.
lines.divide_fractions: Dividing by {b} is the same as times its flip, {flip}: {a} × {flip} = {result}.
lines.divide_zero: {number} ÷ 0 can't be done. No number times 0 makes {number}.
lines.order_note: Times and divide go first, then plus and minus.
lines.already_simplest: {fraction} is already as simple as it gets.
lines.long_repeats: Remainder {rem} again - we've been here before, so the digits repeat from here.
lines.long_more: And so on, the same way.

point_bubbles.about: 2026-10-23 (operator: "thought bubbles are not reiterating their respective value points * brobots to reiterate their value points brobot party style * I need a templated answer-chain mechanism * either the machine (game-mechanism) f*ck*ng works or it doesn't, regardless of the editable data"): the answer chain's point_bubbles part - a value point with notes (title | note | note) becomes his thought bubbles, in order: a hype line for its title, then one party line per note. The model is asked for exactly that (prompt: {title} {notes} {count} {numbered}); a line it misses, or one that shares no word with its note, is made from the note (fallback: {title}, {note}, {Note}; hype: a Brobot's own interjection after a made title line). keep_lead_lines: his own lines before the point's (the weather comment) kept first.
point_bubbles.prompt: Party on your value point, {title}. Answer in exactly {count} short lines, one per line, in this order: a hype line naming {title}; then one line for each - {numbered}. Each line uses its own words from that note, said your way.
